name: BERT Encoder Transformer
description: Every token attends to every other

data.noteContent:
What separates an encoder from a decoder-only stack is what each position may look at. An encoder layer runs one unmasked self-attention pass, so token 3 sees token 15 and the other way round. That makes the representation good for classifying a sentence and useless for generating one left to right.

There is no CLS token here: Mean over the sequence pools the 16 positions instead, and Linear turns that into two class scores. The input is a random tensor, so this graph shows the wiring and the shapes, not a trained model.

編碼器和 decoder-only 堆疊的差別，在於每個位置可以看到什麼。編碼器層做的是一次沒有遮罩的自注意力，所以第 3 個 token 看得到第 15 個，反過來也一樣。這樣的表示很適合替整句分類，卻不能拿來從左到右生成。

這裡沒有 CLS token：改用 Mean 沿序列維度把 16 個位置平均起來，再由 Linear 變成兩個類別分數。輸入是隨機張量，所以這張圖看的是接線與形狀，不是訓練好的模型。

nhead 4 splits d_model 48 into four heads of 12 dimensions each; num_layers 4 stacks the block four times. Those two numbers, not the sequence length, are what make an encoder wide or deep.

nhead 4 把 d_model 48 分成四個頭、每個頭 12 維；num_layers 4 則是把同一個區塊疊四次。決定編碼器寬或深的是這兩個數字，不是序列長度。

dim 1 is the sequence, because to_batch_first has just made the tensor (batch, seq, d). Averaging every token is the simplest sentence vector; BERT itself reads position 0, a token it was trained to fill.

dim 1 是序列維度，因為 to_batch_first 剛把張量轉成 (batch, seq, d)。把所有 token 平均是最簡單的句向量；BERT 本身讀的是第 0 個位置，那是它訓練時就學著填的 token。
